sources.bodyExcerpt: MXR® TIMMY® OVERDRIVE - Dunlop Toggle menu Compare --> Register I Sign in Search Bag Search Close Products --> All Products --> --> Electronics MXR Cry Baby Way Huge Dunlop Electronics Authentic Hendrix Pedal Parts Electronic Parts Legacy Products Guitar Picks Tortex Nylon Max-Grip Jazz Herco Gator Grip Celluloid Ultex Primetone Delrin 500 Flow Finger Thumb Stubby Variety Packs Artist Series Graphic Artist Series Pick Tins Other Clearance Accessories Capos Slides Tonebars MXR Cables Care Maintenance Strap Retainer Straps Tuners Pick Holders GrooveTech Tools Accu-Fret Fretwire Clearance Strings Artist Series Electric Bass Acoustic Classical Americana Ukulele Apparel Shirts Hoodies Hats Artists Lifestyle Sign in MXR® TIMMY® OVERDRIVE CSP027 Description This pedal provides a huge, responsive range of gritty and textured tones that enhance the sound of your rig while preserving its fundamental character—and in an MXR mini housing, this pedal will free up some serious pedalboard space. This pedal is powered by the Dunlop ECB003 9-volt adapter or an MXR Brick Series power supply. This pedal cannot be powered by a battery. Warranty Information The Long Story The MXR Timmy Overdrive provides a huge range of gritty, textured tones that enhance your rig's sound while preserving its fundamental voice—and in an MXR mini housing, it'll free up serious pedalboard space. The pedal's based on a design from veteran pedal builder Paul Cochrane that's widely celebrated among high level pros, from first-call Nashville player Kenny Greenberg to first-call L.A. player Lyle Workman to rockstar Brad Whitford. When Paul decided to bring his pedal to a wider audience, he chose to work with the MXR design team. "It's an honor to work with MXR," Paul says. "My first ever pedal was a Phase 90." Thanks to Paul's inventive implementation of clipping options and tone controls, the Timmy Overdrive is a dream come true for working guitar players. The Clip switch provides three different clipping styles for a multitude of scenarios, whether you need a big, bold always-on sound with a ton of headroom to slam the front end of your amp, a more compressed and saturated sound for fat chords, or anything in between. The Bass and Treble controls offer further refinement in two key ways. First, they're cut-only, keeping your signal's character intact while making it super easy to dial in a clean boost. Second, Paul wired the Bass control to affect your pre-OD signal—so that you can maintain your low end at lower Gain settings—and the Treble control to affect your post-OD signal so that you can adjust the top end to keep dirty settings smooth and musical. Finally, the MXR design team worked with Paul to select an op-amp that perfectly complements his expertly crafted design. They chose the LF353, a component well-respected by Dunlop engineers for providing high output, high gain, and hi-fi signal delivery. The resulting MXR Timmy Overdrive is a professional-grade must-have for players who want sweet, harmonic breakup that responds to playing dynamics and maintains a rig's personality at a fraction of the standard pedal size. sources.bodyExcerpt: MXR Timmy Overdrive Pedal Review: Worth It? Skip to content The Guitar Side Home Gear Reviews Tone Guides Comparisons Guitarists Beginner Guides About The Guitar Side Toggle Menu Gear Reviews MXR Timmy Overdrive Review: Transparent Drive That Actually Stacks By The Guitar Side January 13, 2026 January 14, 2026 If you’re the kind of player who spends more time actually playing than chasing the “perfect” overdrive on YouTube, you’ll get the MXR Timmy immediately: it’s built for real rigs, real rooms, and the small EQ fixes that make a pedalboard work night after night. The MXR Timmy is a rare overdrive that doesn’t try to “win” by imposing a big signature mid-hump or heavy compression. Instead, it’s built around a simple promise: keep your guitar and amp character intact, then let you shape what gets cut and what gets pushed. This MXR Timmy Overdrive pedal review is written for normal players using real setups—clean platforms, edge-of-breakup combos, pedalboard rigs, and rehearsal/gig volumes. I’ve used Timmy-style drives before and know exactly where they shine (stacking, tightening lows, taming harshness) and where they don’t (instant mid-hump solo voice, high-gain saturation). I’m not including audio/video demos here, so I’m focusing on what matters in practice: how it reacts, how it sits in a mix, how to dial it fast, and when to skip it. If you’re still deciding what type of drive fits your board overall, this guide helps: best overdrive pedal for guitar . What you’ll get from this guide: Who the MXR Timmy Overdrive is actually for, and who should skip it. A clear Cochrane Timmy vs MXR Timmy explanation (so SERP confusion doesn’t waste your time). How the EQ behaves and what the knobs actually do in real life. Best Timmy OD settings for clean boost, low gain, and stacking. Simple signal chain recipes you can copy in 60 seconds. In this MXR Timmy review Who the MXR Timmy Overdrive pedal is actually for Quick decision table: should you buy it? Cochrane Timmy vs MXR Timmy: what’s the difference? MXR Timmy specs and controls at a glance How to use the Timmy OD (micro dial-in guide) Tone and feel in the real world Best MXR Timmy settings (fast presets) Home, rehearsal and gig volume behavior Stacking: Timmy overdrive with other drives Buying checklist: MXR Timmy vs alternatives When the MXR Timmy is the wrong choice Summary: is the MXR Timmy Overdrive worth it? MXR Timmy Overdrive FAQ Short version: the MXR Timmy Overdrive is a low-to-mid gain “transparent” overdrive timmy-style pedal with powerful EQ control. It’s especially strong as an always-on tone shaper, a clean-to-gritty boost, and a stacking tool because it doesn’t force a big mid-hump. MXR Timmy Overdrive: pros and cons at a glance Pros Transparent character: keeps your amp and pickups sounding like themselves. Powerful EQ: easy to tame harsh amps or tighten flubby lows. Excellent for stacking: works before or after other drives without turning messy. Great as an always-on foundation or a “make everything better” light drive. Cons If you want a big mid-hump “solo push,” a TS/SD-1 style pedal may feel easier. (Here’s a practical reference point: Ibanez TS9 review .) Not built for modern high-gain saturation by itself. Transparent drives can feel “too subtle” if your amp tone is already uninspiring. Quick decision: does the MXR Timmy Overdrive fit your situation? Three clipping modes, cut-only EQ controls, and LF353 op-amp for pure amp character. admin 22 September 2026 22 min read Updated 24 September 2026 GG-ARTICLE-TOP Most overdrive pedals have a personality. The Ibanez TS9 Tube Screamer pushes mids. The Boss BD-2 Blues Driver bites. The classic Silicon Fuzz Face squashes and spits. They all leave a fingerprint on your tone, and for a lot of music, that’s exactly what you want. But what if you’ve spent years and thousands of dollars building a rig that sounds exactly like you — the guitar, the amp, your hands — and what you need is a pedal that enhances that without changing it? That’s the problem the Timmy was born to solve. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO Paul Cochrane is a Nashville-based pedal builder who, for years, built his Timmy overdrives one at a time by hand. No website. Minimal social media. Waiting lists that stretched for months. And yet the pedal wound up on the boards of Aerosmith’s Brad Whitford, L.A. session legend Lyle Workman, first-call Nashville guitarist Kenny Greenberg, and Alice in Chains’ Jerry Cantrell. Not because anyone was paying to put it there — because the pedal earned its place through sheer sonic integrity. When MXR brought Cochrane into their design facility to translate his circuit into mini-enclosure production format as the MXR Timmy Overdrive (CSP027) , the result was one of the most celebrated OD pedals of the last decade. Here’s everything you need to know about it. How to Get the Tone ↓ The Paul Cochrane Story: Building Cult Status One Pedal at a Time Paul Cochrane’s path to pedal-building legend is the opposite of a marketing campaign. He built pedals because he wanted something specific and couldn’t buy it. The original Timmy — the single-channel version of his Tim pedal (which added a second channel for boost) — circulated through Nashville’s session community on reputation alone. Players who got their hands on one held onto it. Players who didn’t were on a list, waiting. What made the Timmy different wasn’t a novel clipping topology or an exotic component. It was a design philosophy: the pedal should enhance your rig’s voice, not replace it. sources.bodyExcerpt: MXR Tom Morello Power 50 Overdrive Review: Is It Worth It for Rage-Style Grit? | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews MXR Tom Morello Power 50 Overdrive Review: Is It Worth It for Rage-Style Grit? By marcus-reeve June 2, 2026 MXR Tom Morello Power 50 Overdrive Review: Is It Worth It for Rage-Style Grit? The MXR Tom Morello Power 50 Overdrive delivers a tightly focused, high-headroom overdrive optimized for aggressive rhythm textures, pinch harmonics, and articulate mid-forward crunch— not vintage blues warmth or transparent boost. It excels in high-gain contexts where note definition and dynamic response matter more than smooth saturation. For guitarists seeking Rage Against the Machine-style riff articulation, tight low-end control, and reliable stage-ready output , it’s a purpose-built tool—not a general-purpose overdrive. It’s less versatile than the Boss SD-1 or Wampler Plexi Drive but more surgically effective for its niche. Build quality is robust, tonal character is consistent across volume changes, and the output section genuinely handles power amp driving duties—but its rigid voicing limits utility for clean-boost or low-gain applications. About the MXR Tom Morello Power 50 Overdrive Released in 2020 as part of Dunlop’s Artist Signature series, the Power 50 is co-developed with Tom Morello and engineered by MXR (a Dunlop subsidiary since 2007). Unlike many signature pedals that repackage existing circuits, this unit departs significantly from MXR’s classic designs—including the popular Micro Amp and OD800. Morello explicitly sought a pedal that could replicate the responsive, punchy, and dynamically sensitive overdrive he used live and on recordings like The Battle of Los Angeles and Renegades of Funk , particularly when paired with a cranked tube amp’s preamp stage 1 . The goal wasn’t “more gain” but more control : tighter bass response, enhanced pick attack clarity, and a midrange contour that cuts through dense mixes without sounding nasal. MXR positioned it as a “power amp overdrive,” distinguishing it from conventional preamp-style overdrives—and that distinction shapes nearly every design decision. First Impressions: Build, Layout, and Initial Setup The Power 50 arrives in a compact, rugged aluminum chassis (118 × 84 × 44 mm), identical in footprint to MXR’s standard mini-format pedals but slightly taller. Its matte black finish resists scuffs, and the rubberized bottom pads prevent slippage. All controls are top-mounted: three knobs (Drive, Tone, Output), a single footswitch (true bypass), and an LED indicator. No battery compartment—power is exclusively via 9V DC (center-negative, 100 mA minimum required). There’s no internal trim pot or mode switch. The layout is minimalist and uncluttered: Drive sits left, Tone center, Output right. The knobs have smooth, precise taper and positive detents at minimum and maximum positions. First-time setup requires no calibration or firmware—plug in, power up, and play. No learning curve emerges from hidden functions or menu navigation because there are none. That simplicity reflects its singular mission. Detailed Specifications Below is a complete spec breakdown with practical context—not just numbers, but what they mean for real-world use: 🎸 Topology: Discrete op-amp-based overdrive circuit with active EQ shaping and buffered output stage ⚡ Power: 9V DC only (no battery option); current draw: 100 mA — requires a robust power supply; daisy-chaining may cause noise or dropout if under-spec 🎛️ Controls: Drive (0–10), Tone (0–10), Output (0–10); all logarithmic-taper pots with ±5% tolerance 🔌 Input/Output: Standard 1/4" mono jacks; input impedance: 1 MΩ; output impedance: 100 Ω — compatible with long cable runs and buffered effects loops 🔊 Max Output Level: +15 dBu into 10 kΩ load — capable of driving power amp inputs directly (e.g., Marshall JCM800 effects loop return) 📉 Frequency Response: 20 Hz–18 kHz (±3 dB

On the inside, it’s got the same guts, custom built for Zakk’s loud, tough, and relentless riffs and leads. It’ll transform your amp into a heavy, chunky crunch machine. The Swedish Maestro lends his name to a new overdrive pedal 04 Sep 2024 by Jef | | | 4,4 / 5,0 | Reading time: 2 min MXR Yngwie Malmsteen Overdrive · Source: MXR Previous Next ADVERTISEMENT The new MXR Yngwie Malmsteen Overdrive pedal has been officially announced, and it looks very similar to one of his previous signature pedals made by Fender. ADVERTISEMENT MXR Yngwie Malmsteen Overdrive This new bright red, two-knob MXR Yngwie Malmsteen Overdrive pedal is the latest signature product for the Swedish guitar maestro . This musician is famous for his ultra-clean, fluid, legato playing style and lightning-fast neo-classical chops. He needs an overdrive pedal that won’t kill his playing brilliance and can translate his precision picking at high volume. Affiliate Links Fender Yngwie Malmsteen MN VW Customer rating: (45) $2,666.00 / £2,369.00 / 2,749.00€ at We all know he uses scalloped fretboards on his Fender Strats and favours loud Marshall amps, but he still uses an overdrive to give his tone that edge. This latest MXR signature overdrive pedal looks suspiciously similar to the signature Fender pedal he released around ten years ago. You are currently viewing a placeholder content from YouTube . To access the actual content, click the button below. Please note that doing so will share data with third-party providers. More Information Unblock content Accept required service and unblock content Less is More This new signature MXR pedal has two controls, Gain and Level , so it could not be any simpler. However, MXR hasn’t said much more about this new effect and why it is specific to Yngwie’s needs. “This pedal is the culmination of 45+ years developing a sound that’s perfect in every possible way. I present to you: the MXR Yngwie Malmsteen Overdrive. Prepare to be amazed.” — Yngwie J. Malmsteen Less is More ADVERTISEMENT Mr Arpeggio This new pedal will be a hit with fans of the Swedish guitarist. If it can help your cranked Marshall amp sing, it could be perfect for players looking to pull off fast arpeggios and break-neck speed runs. Affiliate Links MXR Randy Rhoads Distortion Customer rating: (1) $219.00 / £195.00 / 225.00€ at Simple Signatures MXR recently launched the highly sought-after Randy Rhoads Distortion +, which has a similar layout and a polka-dot finish. This shows that sometimes, a simple pedal is all you need to give your guitar tone that edge. This latest signature pedal is available in standard red and a limited edition yellow finish. We stand by our work and want to get your pedal working right! This warranty is voided if any modifications are performed on the pedal or outside party repairs are attempted. When in doubt, reach out to us first and we’ll get it all figured out! In certain cases where a pedal is damaged from user error and a repair is possible, we can evaluate the issue and charge a small fee to repair. All repairs and warranty replacements are subject to parts availability. For further details contact us at https://mythospedals.com/pages/contact The 1347 Silicon Fuzz. Built exclusively for Mass Street Music the 1347 is a Mythos homage to those round blue fuzzes that graced stages and studios in the late 1960's. The 1347 takes that classic two transistor fuzz box and puts the Mythos spin on. Mythos has tightened up the low end so that it will play well with a variety of guitar pickups, tweaked the gain so there is plenty of output and a wider range of gain from the fuzz pot and chosen a specific pair of transistors and bias pot to allow for a multitude of fuzz tones. Inside this fuzz are two NOS PN2396A Transistors that are relatively low gain but hand measured and chosen for their specific position to give you all the gnarly fuzz tones while allowing for a remarkable cleanup that doesn't get as thin as some other pedals of this type. The voicing is somewhere between what you'd expect from a germanium and silicon fuzz and it stacks well with a driven amp or a dirt pedal after it. The signal path features high quality WIMA Nichicon Audio grade caps as well as new production Carbon Comp resistors for tight tolerances and low noise. On the underside of the PCB Mythos has gone to great lengths to reduce noise and keep this pedal as stable as possible. Technical Specs Blue Hammertone finish with Iridescent Rainbow Sparkle Top Coat (it’s insane looking in real life!) Stacks great with overdrive pedals Tighter less boomy low end for more focused sound Classic glassy clean up Hand matched silicon transistors Internal Bias trimmer with test points Quality through hole components True Bypass switching Enclosure size: 4.70” x 3.70” x 1.39” Quick links Retired Models Search Former Dealers Contact Blog Plug In! For further details contact us at https://mythospedals.com/pages/contact Designed with That Pedal Show Mick Taylors Idealized Argo Pedal Unlock the Argo circuit The original Argo design is a tweak on the iconic "COB" circuit which allows players the freedom to balance out the Octave Fuzz sounds with a boosted Clean signal. When you set the Fuzz control and Blend control to minimum the Argo circuit functions as a very useful and musical sounding Booster. When Mick Taylor from That Pedal Show approached me about having that be a switchable feature I was excited to be able to derive more from a circuit that so many players know and love. Changing Lanes At its core the Argo Boost Deluxe is the same topology as the Argo, but the additional Footswitch and Red Boost Knob allow players to use the boost portion of the circuit by itself. Instead of pairing a new booster inside this new pedal, think of it as changing lanes inside the pedal. This allows you to have a pair of gain stages that are perfect in front of a drive pedal or drive amp. The boost lets you increase the overall push, and with the push of the FUZZ footswitch you can unleash the full Argo Octave Fuzz sound. Just a little Sparkle Inside the Argo Boost Deluxe there is a HIGHS switch that allows for some more tonal possibilities. In the initial planning for this pedal, Mick has expressed interest in making the boost portion a little brighter overall. Instead of making it a permanent sonic change, we decided to allow players the choice. The pedal ships stock with the HIGHS switch off. The small switch, when engaged, will add a fine amount of high end sparkle to your signal when using the Boost mode. This bright circuit is not part of the Octave Fuzz sound. Mythos x TPS Argo Boost Deluxe March 2025 - Mick here, hello! You might have seen prototypes of this on my board in recent months… and finally it's in production! This amazing two-in-one, full-range boost and blendable octafuzz is a collaboration with Zach and the team at Mythos pedals , as an evolution of the much-loved Argo. Two-In-One Clean Boost OctaFuzz Welcome to the Argo Boost Deluxe! It's a two-in-one full-range boost and blendable octafuzz effect for guitar. The boost side – the red knob and right-hand switch – offers a full range boost that does all the things any great boost pedal will do. You can use to lift your clean tone into a clean amp… or you can boost into other pedals or a dirty amp for extra overdrive and distortion… or you could place it after other overdrives for a solo boost lift. You might also just love it as a super simple always-on boost for more oomph, excitement and dynamics in your core tone. The three white knobs and the left-hand switch add in an octafuzz effect. Originally inspired by the now classic COB fuzz pedal, Zach at Mythos made the fuzz a little more aggressive with some higher-gain transistors and made sure there's a TON of volume on tap. The blend control enables you to have anything from a very subtle amount of octafuzz, through to full-on, fuzzed out octa mayhem. Mick loves the Doyle Bramhall approach, but you can conjure some fantastic Hendrix and Sambora textures too. Inside is a set-and-forget brightness boost switch for the boost side. This might be useful if you have a darker sounding guitar/amp, or if you just want it brighter! Mick likes it off, but you may well prefer it on. BUY HERE MEET THE MAKERS MYTHOS PEDALS The vision behind Mythos is simple: create straightforward, great-sounding effects that anyone can enjoy. ​ Mythos Pedals was founded by Zach Broyles in 2010, born out of a passion for building pedals for himself and his friends. ​ Based just outside of Nashville, Tennessee, Mythos is run by a small, dedicated team of musicians who live and breathe tone. Every pedal is crafted with a deep love for guitar and sound. ​ Zach's journey began in the mid-2000s, when he started modifying existing effects. That curiosity quickly turned into a deeper dive—learning the ins and outs of how pedals work, and eventually designing his own circuits from the ground up. ​

The Big Puft is a homage to the incredible BMP fuzz circuit we all know and love – with a unique Mythos twist. Sonically Zach and the team have tweaked the circuit to have a full and more mid-forward voice, so the days of getting lost in the mix with this style of fuzz are long gone. The Tone knob on the Big Puft has been tuned so at noon you have a much flatter EQ sound, but once you reduce or increase the knob you immediately find some of those classic fuzz sounds this style of pedal is known for. Like all Mythos pedals we strive to make every knob have the best possible function and taper. The Sustain control has a wide array of gain sounds, so you can take the Big Puft to mellow and smooth to searing levels of fuzz. It does it all! While inspired by the iconic BMP circuit, the Puft is sort of an amalgam of our favorite sounds that style pedal has offered. Inspired by a legend The Chupacabra takes its tonal inspiration from the biggest little band from Texas. Utilizing a CMOS Hex chip the Chupacabra has huge amount of output and gain range for a versatile drive that melds perfectly with you guitar setup. The gain ranges from tweed push to "your amp about to die" for some pseudo fuzz-like tones. Tonally, the voicing is pretty flat with a slight bump to lows and highs without being to drastic. Simplicity is Key The Chupacabra CMOS Overdrive is made for those that love using their guitar controls. It's responsive and dynamic and doesn't get in your way. Like all other Mythos Pedals we use high quality panel mount In, Out and DC jacks so your pedal will be reliable on the road for years to come. Chupacabra Controls Volume - Adjusts the output. We found a stash of these enclosures! Some were open so we're selling these all as blems. The Herculean is an incredibly versatile overdrive and designed to capture the best personalities of Zach's favorite overdrive circuits. With it's independent Clarity and Bass knobs you can get classic TS style smokey drive sounds, clear present tones, and everything in between. The Herculean has a huge range of Volume and Gain as well so you can find a place with any guitar/amp setup. This version features a design reminiscent of the most iconic amplifiers of all time. -- The Original Herculean V2 Description The original Herculean was one of the first pedals we introduced and the V2 is the culmination of everything we loved from the original and all we've learned in the past 10 years. For this 4 knob overdrive went back to the drawing board, removing what we deemed unnecessary from the original and tweaked the functions we loved. Herculean V2 covers a lot of ground sonically, from a fat booster to pushed OD to some quasi D-style amp tones (if we may be so bold). In addition to your standard volume and gain controls you have a Clarity and Bass control. The Clarity knob is your "Transparency" control, go from a darker smoky tone reminiscent of classic green dirt boxes, or clear and ringing tones that help lift darker guitars up in the mix. The Bass control set to 0 you have that classic slight bass cut, set to noon it has a nice full low end, and as you increase from there you add low end and really thicken up your gain sound. The tonal combinations are huge and work well for almost any playing style. Top Mount Jacks Great for as a “clean-ish” booster Wide range of gain sounds. The Clarity allows you dial in just the right amount of Transparency. Bass control allows you to add in just enough low end. Don't be afraid to set it fully counter-clockwise! Top quality jacks, switch, pots, and components throughout. Approx. 10 mA Current Draw Grab another deal before they are gone! For further details contact us at https://mythospedals.com/pages/contact It was just a matter of time Inspired by the most iconic pedal of all time Tweaked just right The Envy Pro Overdrive is inspired by the various versions of that ever polarizing green stompbox. We aren't trying to reinvent the wheel, but give you the best that this circuit has to offer. With its increased output, expanded drive range, and thickened low end, the Envy takes the TS formula and makes it more useful for every player, regardless of style. Push it real good We wanted to give the Envy more options than just 3 knobs and decided on something fun and slightly different - push buttons! The Lows and Clip buttons offer quick adjustments of the circuits most oft tweaked parameters. With the buttons up the circuit is a more traditional voiced TS style drive. With Lows engaged you increase the amount of low end for a fuller overall sound. When the Clip button is pushed the diodes are disengaged for a louder, less compressed, more open sound. Through Hole Heart At the core of the Envy Pro Overdrive is a socketed RC4558P Dual Op Amp chip. We did this for one very important reason, experimentation. Zach has said on many occasions that Dual Op Amps don't sound all that different but if you want to experiment with different chips you can do that in the Envy pretty painlessly. RC4558, JRC4558, TL072, OP275, OPA2604, LM1458N the list goes on! Envy Pro Overdrive Controls Level - Adjusts the Output Tone - Classic TS Style Tone Circuit Drive - Adjust the amount of Overdrive Push Switches Lows - Classic Low End (When Up), Increased Low End (When Pushed Down) Clip - Stock TS Soft Clipping (When Up), Diode Lift (When Pushed Down) Recommended Settings Flooding in Texas Grab your Strat and crank it Nice 'N Thick Push the Lows and take a solo There Is No Plan B Push the Lows and Clip for that signature RS sound. The "Extra Spicy" Version of the Extra Hot! Just like when hot sauces dress the bottles up in black/yellow/orange we wanted to heat to the aesthetic of our Extra Hot overdrive. Sonically these have been updated for a more versatile Size (Bass) control, but the rest of the pedal is the same as it was. These will drop in batches occasionally, and are exclusive to mythospedals.com From the Original Extra Hot The Extra Hot is the spiritual successor to the Hot Chicken * pedal we made a number of years ago with a handful of changes. The updated Extra Hot has two different circuits than the OG unit. The Left "Dine In" side features our take on the ever popular ODR sound. This side features Cut (Tone) and Size (Bass) controls that let you shape the voice to fit any setup. We have dabbled in the circuit in the past with the Erlking, but we wanted to reduce the high end and make it a bit more approachable. The "Take Out" side is an updated version of the drive from our Air Lane Drive/ 210 Double Drive pedals. The Flavor control allows you to adjust the Gain with the Sauce being a Volume control. The Take Out side is a simple single transistor, hard clipped overdrive that can be a boost, a low gain drive, to an almost fuzz like dirt pedal. Combining both sides yields a huge variety of sounds in a easy to use dual format. We found that all the bells and whistles one might expect from a two-in-one were NOT necessary in this box. This dual drive is made to plug in, crank, and play. Both sides work independently, but there is no order switcher on the Extra Hot. sources.title: Golden Fleece Fuzz – Mythos Pedals
sources.description: The Golden Fleece is an incredibly simple circuit that skirts the line between overdrive and fuzz. This one knob unit lives in your guitars volume and tone controls. The Golden Fleece cleans up better than almost any other fuzz out there and the single knob on the unit is a master volume control. The unit has a very balanced tone that doesn't shift your guitars sound just offers a biting, yet full sound that would work for a variety of musical styles.

Never in the way Inspired by a little known fuzz box called the "Fuzzy Nuts" (no we're not making that up) the Golden Fleece is a do it all dirt box that perfectly blends Fuzz, Distortion, and Overdrive into one little golden box of fun. The single "More" knob only controls the output of the circuit so it's up to your fingers and guitars controls to shape the gain level and voice. With everything dimed it's a powerful blooming fuzz sound that sounds great hitting a pushed amplifier. Hit the NOS Internally the Golden Fleece is a different type of one knob fuzz. The pedal doesn't rely on a pair of transistors for fuzz instead utilizing a very special silicon and germanium diode pair. Zach has chosen a very special NOS Germanium diode that gives the Golden Fleece its unique and versatile fuzz voice. There are no other internal settings, pots, switches or anything. The philosophy behind this pedal is that you just turn your mind off and play your guitar. Vintage Quirks Just like so many other fuzzes before it the Golden Fleece does have its fair share of quirks. It's best before buffers, that includes buffered tuners, buffered effect loops of switching systems, etc. Buffers will kill the response and drastically change the voice of the pedal. Likewise the Golden Fleece is sensitive to power and signal so use a high quality isolated power supply and good cables for the best tonal experience. Golden Fleece Controls More - Controls the output of the pedals. The rest is up to you. Qty Add to Cart Description What was initially a limited model, the Hephaestus Variable Voltage Fuzz is now a standard model in mini form! Sometimes you dont know where a circuit will take you, such is the story with the Hephaestus. This fuzz box started life as the now legendary Jordan Bosstone, but as Zach attempted to make the pedal more useful he stumbled upon something he didnt expect. The Bosstone circuit is a relatively simple circuit combining a NPN and PNP transistor pair to get some pretty great classic fuzz tones. However the variety of tones in the original units are fairly limited. Zach was bound and determined to find something more interesting and after poking and prodding we landed on something we think people may not expect. Enter the WARNING knob. The WARNING knob on the face of the pedal does not control volume, it doesnt control gain, it controls voltage feeding the circuit! When maxed out the circuit sounds like the best of the classic circuit, but as you turn the knob down and adjust the overall voltage entering the circuit. Once the knob hits 1 oclock something magical happens, a sub octave begins to be introduced! When and where it appears will be very dependent on your guitar and amp setup but it creates a sub octave synth effect that is unlike anything weve ever tried from a simple analog device. Further reducing the voltage or WARNING knob will cause even more octave things to happen while reducing the overall gain of the circuit. Internally there is a master volume so you can adjust the overall output of the pedal. Be warned, this circuit is loud! From us the master will be set at 50% so as to not worry friends and family around you who may bear witness to the first riffs heard from this little red fuzz box.Its weird, wacky, but most importantly its incredibly fun to play. We cannot seem to stop writing riffs on these pedals as we test them and we cannot wait to see what players come up with. sources.bodyExcerpt: Your Klon Search is Over | Mythos Pedals Joey Landreth Mjolnir Overdrive — Edge of Breakup 0 Skip to Content LATEST VIDEOS ABOUT Join the Email List Open Menu Close Menu Open Menu Close Menu LATEST VIDEOS ABOUT Join the Email List LATEST VIDEOS ABOUT Join the Email List Your Klon Search is Over | Mythos Pedals Joey Landreth Mjolnir Overdrive Guitar Pedals Jul 26 Written By Edge of Breakup . Mythos Pedals Joey Landreth Mjolnir Overdrive A Nashville friendship, a Klon-style circuit, NOS germanium diodes, and a sparkle orange finish that makes every other overdrive on your board jealous. Welcome back to Edge of Breakup. In this episode, the Mythos Pedals Joey Landreth Mjolnir Overdrive takes center stage — running into my Kauer Guitars Electroliner loaded with Lollar Sixty-Four Stratocaster pickups, into my 1957 Fender Tweed Princeton 5F2-A with a 12" speaker. The Mjolnir is Mythos Pedals builder Zach Broyles' deeply considered take on the modern classic Klon Centaur circuit — tweaking the clipping for consistency and a slight boost in clarity, while preserving everything that made the original a landmark piece of overdrive design. Like the Klon, it runs internally at 18V despite accepting standard 9V DC, and uses buffered bypass so your signal receives a boost in clarity even when the pedal is switched off. At low gain settings it functions as a supremely transparent, enormously loud clean boost — at higher gain settings it delivers a rich, dynamic overdrive voice that accents your rig without ever taking anything away from it. The Joey Landreth edition is something more personal than a standard Mjolnir. The story begins in 2014, when Zach met Joey Landreth — killer guitarist, fantastic vocalist, master of tone — at The Basement in Nashville, Tennessee. They immediately started talking tone and became fast friends. The very first Mjolnir Zach built for Joey featured vintage NOS germanium diodes, and Joey loved it enough that it became his reference point for what a K-Style overdrive should feel like. The Joey Landreth edition is a replica of that pedal — inspired by and faithful to the original unit Joey has been running ever since. Handmatched NOS germanium clipping diodes give it a beautiful compression when the gain is pushed, and a clarity and personality that is measurably more mellow, softer clipping, and smoother than the standard Mjolnir variants. Limited to just 60 pedals worldwide, hand assembled by Zach and Morgan Broyles in Nashville, Tennessee, in a translucent sparkle orange finish with cream Bakelite-style knobs and an orange LED. Into a 5-watt, single 6V6, Class A tweed Princeton circuit and the pre-CBS Alnico clarity of Lollar Sixty-Four single coils, the Joey Landreth Mjolnir finds a natural home. Its transparency and touch sensitivity reward a light touch and punish nothing — and its buffered bypass means it's quietly improving your signal even when it's off. This is a pedal built around a friendship and a shared obsession with tone. It sounds exactly like that. A tweaked version of an icon. Made for every pedalboard. Ready for every player The Mjolnir is our take on the iconic "Horsey-Man" pedal. Since 2010 we've been perfecting this circuit to work for everyone regardless of taste or preference. The Mjolnir has a bit less gain, less mid honk, and more low end push compared to other "klones". The iconic parts of the circuit remain to make it truly standout in the wide world of pedals. Gig Ready The Mjolnir has some features that make it a bit more pedalboard friendly. We removed the charge pump from this circuit so there is less risk of frying the pedal with incorrect power. This gives the drive a slightly smoother sound as the op-amps clip and help push the hard clipped diodes. We use high quality panel mount In, Out and DC jacks so your pedal will be reliable on the road for years to come. Polish your clean tone The now iconic buffered bypass of this circuit remains so it vastly improves the signal quality of long cable runs or big pedalboards. Just like its inspiration the Mjolnir's Gain control is a dual ganged pot that controls both the clean mix and the gain. At minimum it is pure clean tone, at maximum it's all gain. Mythos Pedals browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal Mythos Pedals The Victor - Distortion Published on December 1, 2025 Mythos Pedals distortion pedal Information The Victor Distortion is a limited edition hard clipping distortion pedal created by Mythos Pedals as a tribute to one of the most iconic distortion circuits in pedal history. Released as a special Black Friday 2025 edition, The Victor is built using through-hole construction with premium components, including Wima capacitors, an OP07CP operational amplifier, and NOS carbon composition resistors. The pedal's design reflects Mythos' focus on high-quality craftsmanship and precision circuit replication while refining the control behavior and tonal balance for improved playability. The Victor delivers the classic aggressive distortion tones of the original inspiration, enhanced with increased low-end response and a smoother taper across its Filter and Distortion controls. These refinements provide a wider tonal range and a more dynamic, touch-sensitive response, making the pedal suitable for a broad range of rock and heavy styles. Built into a custom bent metal enclosure finished in purple and equipped with top-mounted jacks, The Victor combines vintage-inspired tone with modern construction reliability. Controls Volume: Sets the overall output level of the pedal. Filter: Adjusts the high-frequency response, shaping the tonal brightness or darkness. sources.bodyExcerpt: The Victor by Mythos Pedals | RockBoard | PedalPedia Skip to main content LOG IN EXPLORE Mythos Pedals The Victor LOG IN TO SUGGEST IMPROVEMENTS DISTORTION Description The Victor is a distortion pedal from Mythos Pedals — a “tribute to one of the most iconic hard-clipping distortion pedals of all time.” The Victor uses a through-hole build with high-quality components including Wima capacitors, an OP07CP chip and NOS carbon comp resistors. It offers Volume, Filter, and Distortion controls, with true bypass switching, quality top-mount panel jacks, and a custom bent metal enclosure. Sonically, the pedal has an improved Filter and Distortion control with a wider range and taper, boosted low-end, and a lower maximum distortion level to make it more responsive and dynamic while retaining the classic aggressive distortion tone inspiration.
